events.price_note: $20; free for students and financially challenged people
events.source_name: Paul Dresher Ensemble / West Oakland Sound Series
events.title: Hummingbird / We Micromanage Infinity
events.why: A West Oakland Sound Series double bill that pairs modular-synth, software, toy-noisemaker and birdcall chaos with a piano, drums and reeds trio—an unusually unbuttoned local Sunday.

events.title: Bloom Where You Are Planted: Film Screening and Discussion
events.why: A small, community-led documentary night with an art activity and post-film conversation—an East Oakland room for a deeper Sunday rather than holiday retail noise.

events.title: Thingamajigs Performance Group at the Do-Over Series
events.why: The Do-Over pairs solo saxophone with Thingamajigs’ expanded cinema, improvised music, handmade electronics, glass, shō and handheld projection—right in the Deliria-adjacent zone.

events.title: FF in SF: A Celebration of 50 Years of Free Expression with Franklin Furnace
events.why: A free live tether between independent publishing, artist books, a reading and performance: Martha Wilson and SFMOMA Library director David Senior survey Franklin Furnace’s 50-year run.

events.title: Paramount Theatre Public Tour
events.why: Guided 90-minute Art Deco theatre access—an easy way to revisit the building details and local history that made the previous Paramount tour a winner.

events.title: Holiday Art & Book Fair
events.why: A real East Oakland community hang rather than a generic craft fair: local makers, books, poetry, youth voices, DJs, live music and an open mic in one room.

events.title: Unsilent Night 2026
events.why: A participatory sound sculpture in which everyone carries one of four tracks on a phone or boombox; campus acoustics turn the walk into a roaming multichannel composition.

events.price_note: Pay what you want; $10 suggested; museum admission is free; bring quarters
events.title: Cybersentics Book Club: Love Testers + Musée Mécanique Tour
events.why: Gray Area’s best current direct match: a critical reading on early love-testing machines, then hands-on testing and reflection inside the Musée Mécanique—a compact history of sensing, spectacle and algorithms.
